c2_bad.why: Unchanged from c1: it prescribes a faceted filter row with popovers, checkbox facets, counts, chips and a mobile filter sheet for a control that is a two-option segmented native radiogroup (CompareSwitch.jsx). Its own avoid_when ('one or two filters') applies, and following it would be a redesign under a low change budget. It is still a CORE record, i.e. the 'what to build' half of the bundle is still wrong.

Still selected although the page has no search field: debounce, result counts, empty-results suggestions and a TV search screen have nothing to attach to. It traces back to the same requirements error (components/primary_jobs mapping 'filters' to search), which c2 did not fix.

Dropped relative to c1, where it was judged relevant and was used ('Tab order in visual order, do not add custom key handling to a native group'). It is the primary carrier of interaction.keyboard_navigation, a critical concept for a sentence that is literally about keyboard reach; a11y-skip-link now carries that tag but only via its <=5-tab-stops clause.

c2_direction_unjustified.why: 'sharp' against a codebase whose --radius token and inspect result are 4-6px (radius=small); minor, and the direction slot itself is null so nothing downstream acts on it.

why: c2 adds a11y-skip-link - the bypass-blocks/reach-distance record whose complete absence c1's RESULTS filed as a knowledge gap, and which describes the fix that was actually shipped (skip link as first focusable, target with tabindex=-1, keep tab stops before the first control <=5) - though it pays for it by dropping a11y-keyboard-operable and leaves both wrong records (comp-filters, search-filter-feedback) in place, so the core half of the bundle would still point an unwary implementer at rebuilding the segmented control.
